thread:
maya: Quick brain dump  we're reconciling Cursor + Stream surfaces across Py/TS/Go. Two new constraints: (1) browsers sometimes must use websocket fallback (no http2/grpc), and (2) we want a small typed error surface for resume/retry logic. Suggestions?

owen: For transports: have a deterministic fallback order per environment: Dedicated/Private -> grpc, Node/browsers capable of http2 -> grpc-web or http2, legacy browsers -> websocket fallback that implements chunked framing. Make this explicit in client config so teams can opt-out.

li: Cursor vs raw token: expose a Cursor object in SDKs that wraps an opaque token. Cursor should implement language-idiomatic iteration (AsyncIterable in TS/Py, struct with Next(ctx) in Go) and provide to_token()/from_token(). We must document token lifetime and possible invalidation.

sam: Prefetch behavior: default to disabled. Expose cursor.prefetch(n, max_bytes=...) opt-in. In browsers default max_bytes low (2MB). Prefetch must be cancellable and bounded; if prefetch overflows bounds SDK should drop oldest prefetched pages and surface a "prefetch_overflow" event.

maya: How about retries for paged endpoints with side-effects? We should rely on server-provided commit markers. Server can return last_committed_token and a resume_supported boolean. SDKs auto-retry only up to last_committed_token for mutating flows; for read-only paging allow full auto-retry.

owen: Error taxonomy proposal: PAGING_TOKEN_INVALID, PAGING_NOT_RESUMABLE, PAGING_COMMIT_CONFLICT, PAGING_PREFETCH_STALE, STREAM_RESUME_UNSUPPORTED. SDKs map these to typed exceptions (Py: classes, TS: error.name + code, Go: sentinel errors).

li: Websocket fallback nuance: the framing must support both Stream and Cursor semantics. For Cursor/unary pages use request/response messages with continuation token fields. For Stream use streaming frames and a final "done" frame with commit info. Keep wire-level types minimal and server-provided to avoid client parsing issues.

sam: Backpressure: Statically document that Stream APIs are pull-driven and SDKs will not buffer unbounded data. For TS/Py AsyncIterator the next() call pulls next chunk. For Go Stream helper return a channel but note it buffers only a small fixed window (e.g., 16 items).

maya: Telemetry + observability: emit resume_attempts, resume_success, prefetch_pages, prefetch_dropped, pages_fetched, transport_used (grpc/http2/websocket). This will help Optimize suggest safe defaults per workload.

owen: Middleware and config: expose retry_policy (none, conservative, aggressive) and allow per-call overrides. Also expose low-level transport_override for unusual infra. Provide a simple default that works for 95% of cases.

li: Edge case: partial page semantics where server-side operations are applied mid-page. Server must either guarantee page boundaries are commit points or mark individual items with commit markers. SDKs must treat pages without commit markers as non-replayable.

sam: UX: hide raw tokens by default. Cursor.to_token() for persistence. Also provide a small helper to detect stale tokens: Cursor.validate(token) which does a cheap server call to assert resumability.

maya: Action items: li to draft Cursor interface sketches for Py/TS/Go, owen to write transport fallback matrix and websocket framing spec, sam to list error codes and SDK exception mapping. I'll open an RFC with these plus a tiny browser websocket PoC. deploy-bot: please add a CI checklist for Cursor token roundtrip tests.

deploy-bot: reminder: open RFC issue and attach PoC artifacts. Tagging @li @owen @sam.
